question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the signed flux

$$
\Phi=\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S
$$

for the vector field

$$
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\langle - z,2 x,- 2 y\rangle.
$$

The parametric surface is

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle u - v,2 u + v + 1,u + v\rangle.
$$

Use the parameter rectangle

$$
-1\le u\le 0,\qquad 1\le v\le 3.
$$

Use the orientation induced by $\mathbf r_v\times\mathbf r_u$. Enter an exact value.

*Hint:* The oriented area vector is

$$
\mathbf N=\mathbf r_v\times\mathbf r_u=\langle -1,2,-3\rangle.
$$

You may use

$$
\Phi=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv.
$$

$\Phi=$ {{flux}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the parametric flux formula with the specified orientation:

$$
\Phi=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv.
$$

Use the supplied oriented area vector $\mathbf N=\langle -1,2,-3\rangle$.

Substitute the surface coordinates into the field:

$$
x=u - v,\quad y=2 u + v + 1,\quad z=u + v.
$$

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\langle - u - v,2 u - 2 v,- 4 u - 2 v - 2\rangle.
$$

Form the three signed dot-product contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1}&=(- u - v)(-1) \\ &=u+v \\ T_{2}&=(2 u - 2 v)(2) \\ &=4 u- 4 v \\ T_{3}&=(- 4 u - 2 v - 2)(-3) \\ &=12 u+6 v \\ &\quad {}+6\end{aligned}
$$

Collect the polynomial terms, writing $g(u,v)=T_1+T_2+T_3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(u,v)&=17 u+3 v \\ &\quad {}+6\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive with respect to $v$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(u,v)&=17 u v+\frac{3 v^{2}}{2} \\ &\quad {}+6 v\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both inner endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=\int_{1}^{3}g(u,v)\,\mathrm dv \\ &=\left[P(u,v)\right]_{v=1}^{v=3}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=34 u+24\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive of $H(u)$ with respect to $u$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(u)&=17 u^{2}+24 u\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both outer endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}\Phi&=\int_{-1}^{0}H(u)\,\mathrm du \\ &=\left[Q(u)\right]_{u=-1}^{u=0} \\ &=7.\end{aligned}
$$

The cross product includes the surface area scale; there is no extra normalization factor.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the parametric flux formula with the specified orientation:

$$
\Phi=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv.
$$

Use the supplied oriented area vector $\mathbf N=\langle 1,1,-1\rangle$.

Substitute the surface coordinates into the field:

$$
x=u,\quad y=v,\quad z=u + v + 1.
$$

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\langle 2 u,2 v,- u - v - 1\rangle.
$$

Form the three signed dot-product contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1}&=(2 u)(1) \\ &=2 u \\ T_{2}&=(2 v)(1) \\ &=2 v \\ T_{3}&=(- u - v - 1)(-1) \\ &=u+v \\ &\quad {}+1\end{aligned}
$$

Collect the polynomial terms, writing $g(u,v)=T_1+T_2+T_3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(u,v)&=3 u+3 v \\ &\quad {}+1\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive with respect to $v$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(u,v)&=3 u v+\frac{3 v^{2}}{2} \\ &\quad {}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both inner endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=\int_{1}^{2}g(u,v)\,\mathrm dv \\ &=\left[P(u,v)\right]_{v=1}^{v=2}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=3 u+\frac{11}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive of $H(u)$ with respect to $u$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(u)&=\frac{3 u^{2}}{2}+\frac{11 u}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both outer endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}\Phi&=\int_{-1}^{1}H(u)\,\mathrm du \\ &=\left[Q(u)\right]_{u=-1}^{u=1} \\ &=11.\end{aligned}
$$

The cross product includes the surface area scale; there is no extra normalization factor.

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the signed flux

$$
\Phi=\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S
$$

for the vector field

$$
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\langle z,x - 1,- 2 y\rangle.
$$

The parametric surface is

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle u + v,u - v,2 u + v + 1\rangle.
$$

Use the parameter rectangle

$$
1\le u\le 2,\qquad 0\le v\le 2.
$$

Use the orientation induced by $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$. Enter an exact value.

*Hint:* The oriented area vector is

$$
\mathbf N=\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\langle 3,1,-2\rangle.
$$

You may use

$$
\Phi=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv.
$$

$\Phi=$ {{flux}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the parametric flux formula with the specified orientation:

$$
\Phi=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv.
$$

Use the supplied oriented area vector $\mathbf N=\langle 3,1,-2\rangle$.

Substitute the surface coordinates into the field:

$$
x=u + v,\quad y=u - v,\quad z=2 u + v + 1.
$$

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\langle 2 u + v + 1,u + v - 1,- 2 u + 2 v\rangle.
$$

Form the three signed dot-product contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1}&=(2 u + v + 1)(3) \\ &=6 u+3 v \\ &\quad {}+3 \\ T_{2}&=(u + v - 1)(1) \\ &=u+v \\ &\quad {}-1 \\ T_{3}&=(- 2 u + 2 v)(-2) \\ &=4 u- 4 v\end{aligned}
$$

Collect the polynomial terms, writing $g(u,v)=T_1+T_2+T_3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(u,v)&=11 u+2\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive with respect to $v$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(u,v)&=11 u v+2 v\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both inner endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=\int_{0}^{2}g(u,v)\,\mathrm dv \\ &=\left[P(u,v)\right]_{v=0}^{v=2}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=22 u+4\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive of $H(u)$ with respect to $u$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(u)&=11 u^{2}+4 u\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both outer endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}\Phi&=\int_{1}^{2}H(u)\,\mathrm du \\ &=\left[Q(u)\right]_{u=1}^{u=2} \\ &=37.\end{aligned}
$$

The cross product includes the surface area scale; there is no extra normalization factor.
